assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged signal corresponds to regular-expression literals in the extension's bundled build output. The visible patterns are short, fixed, linear expressions used to validate small strings such as character names, reserved filenames, and control characters. None of the visible patterns combines nested or ambiguous quantifiers that could produce catastrophic backtracking, and the scanner retained no matched literal demonstrating otherwise. The inputs are short, user-typed names, and even a slow match would at most stall the user's own tab. No attacker-controlled path to meaningful concrete harm is demonstrated.

In the code shown, these patterns are simple name checks, such as rejecting reserved filenames or control characters. They run instantly on short text and are part of normal character management. Nothing in the evidence shows a way for anyone to cause real harm with them.

assessments.technical_explanation: This correlation rule flags co-occurrence of a network primitive and a dynamic-execution-capable API within the same bundled file. Responses are parsed as structured data and rendered after HTML escaping or sanitizer processing. No path is shown in which retrieved content is passed to code evaluation, and no external destination or credential-bearing request appears in the evidence.
